summary.intent: Clear the entire open-issue backlog for cipher-box by launching as many parallel, non-colliding PR workstreams as possible, then unattended-manage a rate-limited (1/hr) CodeRabbit review queue overnight while the user was AFK, and finally sequence-merge the resulting PRs safely.
summary.outcome: Recon mapped 59 unblocked issues; 10 wave-1 PRs were planned and 5 were shipped (#1021, #1022, #1023, #1024, #1027), closing 19-24 issues including #719, plus 10 new tracking issues (#1014-#1020, #1025, #1026, #1028, #1029) minted with verified dependency edges. All five PRs merged to main after resolving two non-textual merge conflicts (api/client.rs helper reshaping, RecordTransport trait signature change); stale issue-number code comments were identified as systemically unreliable (317/365 references pointing at closed issues) and being scrubbed in favor of verifiable state claims.

repo: crates/engine/src/facade.rs and crates/engine/tests/write_plane.rs are hotspots touched by nearly every engine PR — the real cap on parallelism, not issue count
Unimplemented facade command arms fall through to `EngineError::Unimplemented` at facade.rs:1901 (Share, Downgrade, CreateInviteLink, AcceptShare, RotateNow, Revoke)
crates/engine/src/rotation/ (~6,300 lines) and grants/ (~2,600 lines) have every named primitive landed and simulation-tested, but nothing is wired to production seams — only fakes exist
gate::floor::check rejects records below the durable epoch floor, which structurally conflicts with the sweep's job of converging exactly those below-floor records (open design question, #1025)

apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs is only 107 lines with zero engine bootstrap — no Engine::start, no SeamSet, no StoragePolicy — this is the real blocker for the desktop chain, not #846's budget number
packages/client/test/browser/ was excluded from the tsconfig the CI Typecheck job runs, letting worker-glue type drift go undetected (#975)
Rate-limited CodeRabbit (1/hr org-wide) edits ONE status comment in place rather than posting a new one — checking too early reads a stale mid-flight state; must re-fetch after the edit timestamp
CodeRabbit CHILL review profile suppresses nitpicks vs ASSERTIVE — zero actionable comments under CHILL is weaker evidence than under ASSERTIVE, especially for crypto-sensitive diffs

git merge-tree can silently miss semantic conflicts even when it reports zero textual conflicts — cross-branch trait signature changes (e.g. RecordTransport::get_record gaining a max_bytes param) compile-break even when both sides merge cleanly textually

Repo convention discovered as unsound: ~86% of `#NNNN` issue-number references embedded in code comments point at already-closed issues (#745/#746 appear 25 times alone) — comments should state verifiable facts ('no production impl; tests fake this'), not ticket numbers, since issues change independently of code and nothing catches the drift

secret_util.rs and ct_eq_32 were deleted in #1021/#998; replaced by core::suite::secret::ct_eq built on subtle::ConstantTimeEq, and SecretBytes now has constant-time PartialEq/Eq — new secret-bearing types should derive over SecretBytes rather than hand-rolling redaction

code.finding: fanout_get_verify's return type changed from (u64, bytes) to (VerifiedRecord, Vec<u8>) in #997/#1021, rippling into liveness.rs, publish.rs, resolve.rs, pointer_fetch.rs, settings.rs, sync/drain.rs

HIGH bug fixed in #1027: write body structure signature was signed at the write epoch while the gate recomputes structure preimages at the read epoch; a read rotation separates the two, so the first production revocation would have signed a permanently unadoptable scope root

RootAdopter hard-coded parent_node_seed: None, which the gate treats as a fail-closed ascent-link mismatch — every interior scope root has an ascent link, so the resolver could never resolve a real descendant; fixed in #1027 by threading reader-derived ancestry
the other => EngineError::Unimplemented fall-through arm covers Share, Downgrade, CreateInviteLink, AcceptShare, RotateNow, and Revoke command dispatch
NaN/Infinity maxBytes bypassed both size-cap comparisons, allowing an untrusted body to drain unbounded despite the cap; fixed with Number.isSafeInteger + non-negative guard at top of drainCapped

the contract crate's Http seam silently dropped request.timeout_ms instead of forwarding it to the reqwest builder, letting calls the engine bounded to CONTROL_TIMEOUT_MS run to the full 30s client budget

reshaped in #1021: request_authed became bodyless, json_authed added, request_authed_with signature changed — later PR #1023 threading timeout_ms/credentials through these helpers required semantic (not just textual) re-resolution on rebase, since json_authed arrived from main outside the conflict hunk and needed a second manual edit to compile

workflow: When fanning out many agents to modify a shared codebase in parallel, run a file-surface recon pass first (per-cluster file-mapping agents) to detect hot files/collisions before launching implementation agents

Resume the same agent (via SendMessage/ToolSearch) for follow-up work like splitting a PR or rebasing, rather than starting fresh — it retains commit-by-commit history and context that fresh git surgery would lack

Brief shipping agents with explicit conflict/collision maps (which functions are changing shape, which files are reserved by other in-flight PRs) so they write new code against the post-merge shape rather than the current one
Re-draft (un-ready) a PR immediately after a review lands with findings, before pushing fixes, so the fix-push doesn't consume the next rate-limited review slot

Mandate that agents run /simplify, /security-review, and /crypto-privacy-review on their own diff before finishing, especially for crypto-touching PRs — these gates caught multiple HIGH-severity bugs before external review ever saw them

When testing multi-PR merge order, textual git merge-tree cleanliness is necessary but not sufficient — also actually compile the combined tree, and enumerate not just literal-construction sites (e.g. struct literals) but also trait-impl sites, since a signature change to a trait method breaks impls that merge-tree won't flag as conflicting
Split a PR by basing the extracted piece on main (not on the original branch) so the focused review isn't gated behind the mechanical work riding alongside it

When declining to blindly apply a reviewer's suggested fix, agents should verify the fix's premise empirically (e.g. determinism claims) and leave the review thread unresolved with reasoning, rather than silently overriding or blindly complying — but user should spot-check these confident refusals
Fast-forwarding local main to origin before launching worktree-based agents is a required precondition
